note: Verbatim quotes, each found on its source page and checked a second time by an independent pass; punctuation normalized (em dashes shown as en dashes, a trailing comma as a period).

quotes.text: probably rat poison squared.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting weekend, as reported by CNBC
quotes.source_title: Warren Buffett says bitcoin is probably rat poison squared
quotes.gist: Bitcoin is worse than worthless: a toxic speculation with no productive value.

quotes.text: I certainly didn't invest in crypto. I'm proud of the fact that I avoided it. It's like some venereal disease.
quotes.speaker: Charlie Munger
quotes.role: Vice Chairman, Berkshire Hathaway; Chairman, Daily Journal Corp.
quotes.context: Daily Journal annual meeting Q&A
quotes.source_title: Charlie Munger: Crypto Is 'Like Some Venereal Disease'
quotes.gist: Crypto is something to be proud of avoiding entirely, not an asset to own.

quotes.text: If you offered me all the Bitcoin in the world, and you offered it to me for $25, I wouldn't take it, because what would I do with it.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting
quotes.source_title: Buffett says he wouldn't buy 'all the bitcoin in the world' for $25
quotes.gist: Bitcoin produces nothing, so even all of it at a token price is not worth owning.

quotes.text: Bitcoin does nothing. I call it the pet rock.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: CNBC interview at the World Economic Forum, Davos
quotes.source_title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says the bank will let clients buy bitcoin
quotes.gist: Bitcoin has no function; it is a fad object like the 1970s pet rock.

quotes.text: The U.S. dollar seems to be rolling over, and gold and silver may be about to start new legs up. If you have any Bitcoin, sell it now and buy gold and silver.
quotes.speaker: Peter Schiff
quotes.role: Chief Economist and Global Strategist, Euro Pacific Asset Management
quotes.context: Post on X, reported by Benzinga
quotes.source_title: Peter Schiff Wants Investors To Ditch Bitcoin For Gold, Silver Which Could 'Start New Legs Up'
quotes.gist: Bitcoin is a false hedge; the real debasement trade is gold and silver.

quotes.text: I think this is the weakest claim being made about Bitcoin. As I said in the memo, "it's not real" - there is no intrinsic value behind it.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Oaktree memo "Yet Again?"
quotes.source_title: Howard Marks Responds to Critics With Memo: 'Yet Again?'
quotes.gist: Bitcoin cannot be appraised as an investment because nothing of intrinsic value backs it.

quotes.text: I don't think you should smoke, but I defend your right to smoke. ... I defend your right to buy bitcoin.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: JPMorgan Chase investor day, announcing clients may buy bitcoin
quotes.source_title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says the bank will let clients buy bitcoin
quotes.gist: Still a bad habit in his view, but clients should be free to own it and JPMorgan will let them.

quotes.text: I doubt that any central bank will take it on as a reserve currency.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: Post on X sharing a Master Investor Podcast clip, reported by Benzinga
quotes.source_title: Ray Dalio Doubts Any Central Bank Would Take On Bitcoin As Reserve Currency Despite Many Seeing It As Alternative Money: 'There's No Privacy'
quotes.gist: Bitcoin's public ledger and code risks keep it from becoming a central-bank reserve asset like gold.

quotes.text: What I don't care for about crypto is, what problem does it solve for our economy?
quotes.speaker: Ken Griffin
quotes.context: New York Times DealBook Summit
quotes.source_title: Ken Griffin says crypto is exploding right now because more people want to have 'agency' in their lives
quotes.gist: Despite regretting missing the rally, he sees no economic problem that crypto solves.

quotes.text: My personal approach is that I do have some Bitcoin in my portfolio, but not much.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: Master Investor Podcast clip, shared on X
quotes.source_title: Ray Dalio Doubts Any Central Bank Would Take On Bitcoin As Reserve Currency Despite Many Seeing It As Alternative Money: 'There's No Privacy'
quotes.gist: A small position is reasonable as an alternative money, but not a core holding.

quotes.text: Thus, I've concluded (with Andrew's help) that I'm not yet informed enough to form a firm view on cryptocurrencies.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Oaktree memo "Something of Value"
quotes.source_title: Something of Value
quotes.gist: A former skeptic concedes his doubts have not borne out and withholds judgment.

quotes.text: I don't own any bitcoin to be frank but I should.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.role: Chairman and CEO, Duquesne Family Office
quotes.context: Fireside chat with Paul Tudor Jones at a New York investor conference
quotes.source_title: Billionaire Druckenmiller calls Bitcoin a 'brand' he should probably own
quotes.gist: Young investors treat bitcoin as a store-of-value brand, so it deserves a place in a portfolio.

quotes.text: At the end of the day, the best profit-maximizing strategy is to own the fastest horse… If I am forced to forecast, my bet is it will be Bitcoin.
quotes.speaker: Paul Tudor Jones
quotes.role: Founder and CIO, Tudor Investment Corp.
quotes.context: Tudor Investment Corp. investor letter, "The Great Monetary Inflation"
quotes.source_title: Paul Tudor Jones makes compelling case for Bitcoin
quotes.gist: Among inflation hedges, bitcoin is likely the best performer in an era of money printing.

quotes.text: Bitcoin should be a good source of diversification for asset allocators looking for higher returns per unit of risk during the years ahead.
quotes.speaker: Cathie Wood
quotes.role: Founder, CEO and CIO, ARK Invest
quotes.context: ARK commentary after bitcoin lagged gold in 2025, reported by Benzinga
quotes.source_title: In 2025, Bitcoin Fell 6% And Gold Rose 65%-But Cathie Wood Says BTC Will Win In 2026
quotes.gist: Bitcoin's low correlation makes it an attractive risk-adjusted diversifier going forward.

quotes.text: If everyone adopted that conversation, it would be $500,000, $600,000, $700,000 per Bitcoin.
quotes.speaker: Larry Fink
quotes.context: Bloomberg interview at the World Economic Forum, Davos
quotes.source_title: BlackRock's Larry Fink points to sign Bitcoin is heading toward $700,000
quotes.gist: If sovereign funds allocated a few percent to bitcoin, the price could reach $700,000.

quotes.text: For me to say that Bitcoin is going to demonetise gold understates it. Yes, it's going to demonetise gold, then it's going to demonetise real estate, which is 10 times more valuable than gold
quotes.speaker: Michael Saylor
quotes.context: Digital Asset Summit, reported by Business Standard
quotes.source_title: Bitcoin's market cap will eventually reach $500 trn, says Michael Saylor
quotes.gist: Bitcoin will surpass gold's market cap and then absorb other long-term stores of value.

quotes.text: Gold, however, has two significant shortcomings, being neither of much use nor procreative.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2011 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. 2011 Shareholder Letter
quotes.gist: Gold produces nothing and has little use, so it cannot compound like productive assets.

quotes.text: I think gold is a great thing to sew into your garments if you're a Jewish family in Vienna in 1939, but I think civilized people don't buy gold. They invest in productive businesses.
quotes.speaker: Charlie Munger
quotes.context: CNBC interview
quotes.source_title: Charlie Munger: Civilized people don't buy gold
quotes.gist: Gold is only for catastrophe; normal investors should own productive businesses.

quotes.text: In our view, the bubble today is not in AI, but in gold.
quotes.speaker: Cathie Wood
quotes.role: Founder, CEO and CIO, ARK Invest
quotes.context: Posts on X, reported by Benzinga
quotes.source_title: Cathie Wood Warns The Real Bubble Is Gold As Robin Brooks Exposes 'Bogus' Central Bank Buying Myth
quotes.gist: Gold's market value relative to money supply is at a record, a bubble a stronger dollar could pop.

quotes.text: (W)ith an asset like gold, for example, you know, basically gold is a way of going long on fear, and it's been a pretty good way of going long on fear from time to time.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: CNBC Squawk Box interview
quotes.source_title: 3 Things Warren Buffett Has Said About Gold
quotes.gist: Gold only pays if fear keeps rising; it is a bet on sentiment, not value.

quotes.text: All the reasons I have owned it for the last couple of years, it seems to me they may be ending. And by the way, they're ending globally.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.role: Chairman and CEO, Duquesne Family Office
quotes.context: CNBC Squawk Box, after selling all his gold on election night
quotes.source_title: Stanley Druckenmiller says all the reasons he's owned gold are ending
quotes.gist: When easy money and growth fears fade, the case for holding gold fades with them.

quotes.text: Gold has become a momentum/meme asset. If you want to own it, wait awhile.
quotes.speaker: Bill Gross
quotes.context: Post on X, reported by Fortune
quotes.source_title: Bill Gross says gold is now a 'momentum/meme asset' and if you really want to buy it, you should wait awhile
quotes.gist: Gold's 2025 run is driven by momentum, so buyers should wait for a pullback.

quotes.text: At $1,710 or whatever it is today I'm not buying gold, I'm just watching.
quotes.speaker: Jim Rogers
quotes.role: Chairman, Rogers Holdings; co-founder, Quantum Fund
quotes.context: CNBC interview; he also said he owns gold and is not selling
quotes.source_title: Jim Rogers Says Gold Due for Correction; Owns Dollar
quotes.gist: A long-term gold holder expects a correction and will not add at high prices.

quotes.text: This is one of the few times in my life it's semi-rational to have some in your portfolio.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: Fortune Most Powerful Women Summit
quotes.source_title: Fortune: Jamie Dimon says it's semi-rational to hold gold in your portfolio
quotes.gist: A self-described non-buyer of gold concedes today's risks make a small allocation reasonable.

quotes.text: Gold is a currency. We think of currencies of being fiat currency, the major fiat currency, but gold is a currency.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: Greenwich Economic Forum
quotes.source_title: Ray Dalio says investors should take heed of the 1970s and increase their gold holdings
quotes.gist: Gold is money outside the fiat system and deserves a larger allocation, around 15%.

quotes.text: I'm 70 years old, I own gold.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.role: Chairman and CEO, Duquesne Family Office
quotes.context: Fireside chat with Paul Tudor Jones at a New York investor conference
quotes.source_title: Billionaire Druckenmiller calls Bitcoin a 'brand' he should probably own
quotes.gist: He holds gold as the 5,000-year-old store-of-value brand.

quotes.text: I'm long gold, I'm long Bitcoin. I think commodities are so ridiculously underowned – so I'm long commodities.
quotes.speaker: Paul Tudor Jones
quotes.role: Founder and CIO, Tudor Investment Corp.
quotes.context: CNBC interview
quotes.source_title: 'All Roads Lead to Inflation' Says Billionaire Bitcoin Bull Paul Tudor Jones
quotes.gist: With deficits pointing to inflation, he is positioned long gold, bitcoin and commodities.

quotes.text: This will place Poland among the elite ten countries with the largest gold reserves in the world.
quotes.speaker: Adam Glapiński
quotes.context: NBP announcement of plan to raise gold reserves to 700 tonnes
quotes.source_title: Poland to increase gold reserve to world's 10th largest
quotes.gist: One of the biggest central-bank buyers keeps adding gold as a core reserve asset.

quotes.text: It could easily go to $5,000 or $10,000 in environments like this.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: Fortune Most Powerful Women Summit
quotes.source_title: Fortune: Jamie Dimon says it's semi-rational to hold gold in your portfolio
quotes.gist: In today's risk environment gold could more than double from around $4,000.

quotes.text: Put it in the closet, put it under the bed, put it somewhere. Everybody should have some gold and silver.
quotes.speaker: Jim Rogers
quotes.role: Chairman, Rogers Holdings; co-founder, Quantum Fund
quotes.context: BullionStar interview
quotes.source_title: Jim Rogers on Why He'll Never Sell His Gold and Silver, the Fate of the Dollar, and the Complacency That Worries Him
quotes.gist: Physical gold and silver are essential insurance as governments debase currencies.

quotes.text: very, very bullish on gold
quotes.speaker: Jeffrey Gundlach
quotes.context: Bloomberg Odd Lots podcast, reported by Fortune
quotes.source_title: 'Bond King' Jeffrey Gundlach says there's no doubt 'we're in a mania,' but gold is a 'real asset class'
quotes.gist: Gold is a real asset class and his top idea, even as he calls other markets a mania.

quotes.text: ...if this doesn't happen, and we have the equivalent of, you know, an economic heart attack, or a heart attack of the bond market, then you know who's responsible, because it can happen.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: CNBC interview at the World Governments Summit, Dubai
quotes.source_title: Ray Dalio to the Trump administration: Cut debt now or face an 'economic heart attack'
quotes.gist: Without deficit cuts the US risks a debt death spiral and a bond-market heart attack.

quotes.text: In this context, the fiscal recklessness of the last decade has been like watching a horror movie unfold.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.role: Chairman and CEO, Duquesne Family Office
quotes.context: Presentation at USC Marshall
quotes.source_title: Stanley Druckenmiller: Fiscal Recklessness Of The Last Decade Like Watching A Horror Movie
quotes.gist: Entitlement growth and a decade of borrowing put US finances on a dangerous path.

quotes.text: We are spending like drunken sailors
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.role: Chairman and CEO, Duquesne Family Office
quotes.context: CNBC Squawk Box interview
quotes.source_title: Stanley Druckenmiller says government needs to stop spending like drunken sailors, cut entitlements
quotes.gist: Federal spending has jumped from 20% to 25% of GDP and must be cut, starting with entitlements.

quotes.text: Paper money can see its value evaporate if fiscal folly prevails. In some countries, this reckless practice has become habitual, and, in our country's short history, the U.S. has come close to the edge.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2024 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter, reported by AP
quotes.source_title: Warren Buffett offers lessons on investing in his annual Berkshire Hathaway letter
quotes.gist: Fiscal irresponsibility can destroy a currency's value, and the US has flirted with it.

quotes.text: If the U.S. doesn't get its debt under control, if deficits keep ballooning, America risks losing that position to digital assets like Bitcoin.
quotes.speaker: Larry Fink
quotes.context: BlackRock annual chairman's letter to shareholders
quotes.source_title: Fortune: Larry Fink letter on bitcoin, the dollar and reserve currency status
quotes.gist: Unchecked deficits could cost the dollar its reserve-currency role.

quotes.text: You're going to see a crack in the bond market.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: Public remarks after Moody's US credit downgrade, reported by Benzinga
quotes.source_title: Jamie Dimon's 5 Most Recent Dire Warnings Include Recession, 'Panic' And Zero Growth
quotes.gist: Huge deficits and complacent central banks will eventually trigger a Treasury market break.

quotes.text: So we're seeing substantial asset inflation away from the dollar as people are looking for ways to effectively dedollarize or de-risk their portfolios vis-à-vis U.S. sovereign risk.
quotes.speaker: Ken Griffin
quotes.context: Citadel conference in New York
quotes.source_title: Fortune: Ken Griffin says America's economy is on a 'sugar high'
quotes.gist: Investors are hedging US sovereign risk by moving into gold and other dollar substitutes.

quotes.text: 10 year Treasury has no business below 4% though 4.5% more like it – too much supply/deficits despite slowing, soon-to-be 1% growth economy.
quotes.speaker: Bill Gross
quotes.context: Post on X, reported by Fortune
quotes.source_title: Bill Gross says gold is now a 'momentum/meme asset' and if you really want to buy it, you should wait awhile
quotes.gist: Heavy Treasury issuance from deficits should keep long yields high even as growth slows.

quotes.text: The solution to too much spending and too much debt is not more spending and more debt.
quotes.speaker: Jim Rogers
quotes.role: Chairman, Rogers Holdings; co-founder, Quantum Fund
quotes.context: CNBC interview
quotes.source_title: Jim Rogers Says Gold Due for Correction; Owns Dollar
quotes.gist: Borrowing more to fix a debt problem only delays and enlarges the reckoning.

quotes.text: I'm going to bet on American business, but I wanna immunize some of my sovereign exposure to the United States.
quotes.speaker: Ken Griffin
quotes.context: Citadel conference in New York, describing investor behavior
quotes.source_title: Fortune: Ken Griffin says America's economy is on a 'sugar high'
quotes.gist: Investors stay bullish on US companies while hedging US government and dollar risk.

quotes.text: What you need to do is cut your deficit from about 7.5% of GDP to 3% of gross domestic product, and you can do that.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: CNBC interview at the World Governments Summit, Dubai
quotes.source_title: Ray Dalio to the Trump administration: Cut debt now or face an 'economic heart attack'
quotes.gist: The debt problem is serious but fixable with a deficit target of 3% of GDP.

quotes.text: This is no surprise given the primacy of the U.S. dollar in global finance and trade, and I believe that stablecoins have the potential to maintain and extend the role of the dollar internationally.
quotes.speaker: Christopher J. Waller
quotes.context: Speech "Reflections on a Maturing Stablecoin Market", San Francisco
quotes.source_title: Reflections on a Maturing Stablecoin Market
quotes.gist: The dollar's primacy is intact, and dollar stablecoins could extend it.

quotes.text: All else equal, this new demand lowers borrowing costs for the U.S. government.
quotes.speaker: Stephen I. Miran
quotes.context: Speech "A Global Stablecoin Glut", on foreign stablecoin demand for Treasury bills
quotes.source_title: A Global Stablecoin Glut: Implications for Monetary Policy
quotes.gist: Global demand for dollar stablecoins is a new buyer of Treasuries that eases US financing.

quotes.text: A year ago everybody was pessimistic about the dollar, including me… when everybody is on the same side of the boat, you go to the other side of the boat for a while.
quotes.speaker: Jim Rogers
quotes.role: Chairman, Rogers Holdings; co-founder, Quantum Fund
quotes.context: CNBC interview, explaining why he owned the dollar
quotes.source_title: Jim Rogers Says Gold Due for Correction; Owns Dollar
quotes.gist: Consensus dollar pessimism is a contrarian reason to own the dollar.

quotes.text: Our unwavering conclusion: Never bet against America.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2020 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. 2020 Shareholder Letter
quotes.gist: America's long-run resilience makes betting against it a losing proposition.

quotes.text: The inflation tax has a fantastic ability to simply consume capital.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Fortune essay "How Inflation Swindles the Equity Investor"
quotes.source_title: Buffett: How inflation swindles the equity investor
quotes.gist: Persistent inflation silently destroys investors' real capital.

quotes.text: an unprecedented expansion of every form of money unlike anything the developed world has ever seen.
quotes.speaker: Paul Tudor Jones
quotes.role: Founder and CIO, Tudor Investment Corp.
quotes.context: Investor letter "The Great Monetary Inflation"
quotes.source_title: Paul Tudor Jones makes compelling case for Bitcoin
quotes.gist: Pandemic money printing set up a great monetary inflation.

quotes.text: All roads lead to inflation – that's historically the way every civilization has got out: they've inflated away their debts.
quotes.speaker: Paul Tudor Jones
quotes.role: Founder and CIO, Tudor Investment Corp.
quotes.context: CNBC interview
quotes.source_title: 'All Roads Lead to Inflation' Says Billionaire Bitcoin Bull Paul Tudor Jones
quotes.gist: Heavy debt loads make inflation the politically chosen way out.

quotes.text: In my base case, further policy adjustments are likely to be needed to ensure inflation comes down to target in a timely fashion.
quotes.speaker: Michael S. Barr
quotes.context: Speech at the Detroit Economic Club, after the FOMC raised rates in September 2026
quotes.source_title: Economic Conditions and Monetary Policy
quotes.gist: After the September 2026 hike, more tightening is likely needed to get inflation down.

quotes.text: Reducing inflation is likely to require a sustained period of below-trend growth.
quotes.speaker: Jerome H. Powell
quotes.context: Jackson Hole speech "Monetary Policy and Price Stability"
quotes.source_title: Monetary Policy and Price Stability
quotes.gist: Beating inflation will take slower growth and some pain.

quotes.text: Once this is past, I would suspect that commodities would continue to go higher and that you would continue to see more inflation.
quotes.speaker: Jim Rogers
quotes.role: Chairman, Rogers Holdings; co-founder, Quantum Fund
quotes.context: CNBC interview
quotes.source_title: Jim Rogers Says Gold Due for Correction; Owns Dollar
quotes.gist: Money printing will keep pushing commodity prices and inflation higher.

quotes.text: Inflation is substantially above target and substantially above target for all forecasts next year.
quotes.speaker: Ken Griffin
quotes.context: Citadel conference in New York
quotes.source_title: Fortune: Ken Griffin says America's economy is on a 'sugar high'
quotes.gist: Inflation is not beaten and forecasts show it staying above target.

quotes.text: The responsibility for 65 months of sustained, elevated inflation sits squarely with the central bank.
quotes.speaker: Kevin Warsh
quotes.context: Jackson Hole speech "In Our Time"
quotes.source_title: In Our Time
quotes.gist: The new Fed chair says inflation is still too high and the Fed must focus on prices.

quotes.text: This is because if the shocks hit one after another, they will keep inflation elevated for quite some time.
quotes.speaker: Christopher J. Waller
quotes.context: Speech "One Transitory Shock After Another", Auburn University, amid the 2026 oil shock
quotes.source_title: One Transitory Shock After Another
quotes.gist: Back-to-back tariff and oil shocks can keep inflation high even if each is temporary.

quotes.text: At the same time, the balance of risks appears to be shifting.
quotes.speaker: Jerome H. Powell
quotes.context: Jackson Hole speech "Monetary Policy and the Fed's Framework Review"
quotes.source_title: Monetary Policy and the Fed's Framework Review
quotes.gist: Upside inflation risk from tariffs is now weighed against rising labor-market risk.

quotes.text: The current policy stance is well positioned to address the risks to both sides of our dual mandate.
quotes.speaker: Philip N. Jefferson
quotes.context: Speech at the Brookings Institution
quotes.source_title: Economic Outlook and Supply-Side (Dis)Inflation Dynamics
quotes.gist: With disinflation stalled by tariffs, policy near neutral balances both risks.

quotes.text: But that concern is tempered by a number of factors that suggest that these elevated readings are likely to prove temporary.
quotes.speaker: Jerome H. Powell
quotes.context: Jackson Hole speech "Monetary Policy in the Time of COVID"
quotes.source_title: Monetary Policy in the Time of COVID
quotes.gist: The 2021 inflation spike was expected to fade on its own, a call later proved wrong.

quotes.text: As I have said many times, tariff increases are a one-time boost to prices that do not sustainably increase inflation.
quotes.speaker: Christopher J. Waller
quotes.context: Speech "The Case for Cutting Now", Money Marketeers of NYU
quotes.source_title: The Case for Cutting Now
quotes.gist: Tariffs lift the price level once, so the Fed can look through them and cut.

quotes.text: US economy today looks nothing like the double-digit inflation-prone 1970s or the deflationary bust of the 1930s.
quotes.speaker: Cathie Wood
quotes.role: Founder, CEO and CIO, ARK Invest
quotes.context: Posts on X, reported by Benzinga
quotes.source_title: Cathie Wood Warns The Real Bubble Is Gold As Robin Brooks Exposes 'Bogus' Central Bank Buying Myth
quotes.gist: Fears of a 1970s-style inflation are misplaced.

quotes.text: My confidence has grown that inflation is on a sustainable path back to 2 percent.
quotes.speaker: Jerome H. Powell
quotes.context: Jackson Hole speech "Review and Outlook", which declared the time had come to cut
quotes.source_title: Review and Outlook
quotes.gist: Inflation was judged beaten enough to start cutting rates.

quotes.text: If deregulation boosts potential output above actual, the correct response is to cut rates.
quotes.speaker: Stephen I. Miran
quotes.context: Speech at the Delphi Economic Forum, Athens
quotes.source_title: Regulations, the Supply Side, and Monetary Policy
quotes.gist: Deregulation is a disinflationary supply boost, so policy should keep easing.

quotes.text: Sometimes, we see bubbles. Sometimes, there is something to do about it. Sometimes, the only winning move is not to play.
quotes.speaker: Michael Burry
quotes.context: Post on X, read as an AI bubble warning
quotes.source_title: 'Big Short' investor Michael Burry is back with a bubble warning after 2 years of silence (Business Insider via AOL)
quotes.gist: The AI boom is a bubble, and the smart move is to stay out or bet against it.

quotes.text: You've gotta hope that changes, because if it doesn't, there's going to be debt defaults on these things.
quotes.speaker: Jim Chanos
quotes.context: Yahoo Finance interview on loss-making neoclouds and AI firms
quotes.source_title: Famed short seller Jim Chanos sees risks in growing debt market backed by Nvidia's AI chips: 'There's going to be debt defaults'
quotes.gist: Loss-making AI and neocloud businesses financed with debt will default unless their economics improve.

quotes.text: The numbers being thrown around are so extreme that it's really, really hard to understand them.
quotes.speaker: David Einhorn
quotes.context: Simplify Asset Management panel at the NYSE
quotes.source_title: Greenlight founder flags potential capital destruction from AI spending boom (Hedgeweek)
quotes.gist: AI capex figures are so large that the returns are hard to justify, risking capital destruction.

quotes.text: every really important new technology has had a bubble around it
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Grantham
quotes.role: Co-founder and long-term investment strategist, GMO
quotes.context: Merryn Talks Money podcast (Bloomberg)
quotes.source_title: Ever-Bearish Grantham Insists AI Is a Bubble Waiting to Pop (Bloomberg via Advisor Perspectives)
quotes.gist: Like railroads and the internet, AI is important but is wrapped in a bubble that will burst.

quotes.text: If that enthusiasm doesn’t produce a bubble conforming to the historical pattern, that will be a first.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo to Oaktree clients, "Is It a Bubble?"
quotes.source_title: Is It a Bubble? (Howard Marks memo)
quotes.gist: History says enthusiasm for a transformational technology almost always produces a bubble, and AI is unlikely to be the exception.

quotes.text: I won't dwell on other glamorous businesses that dramatically changed our lives but concurrently failed to deliver rewards to U.S. investors: the manufacture of radios and televisions, for example.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Fortune essay based on his Sun Valley remarks
quotes.source_title: Mr. Buffett on the Stock Market (Fortune, 1999)
quotes.gist: Technologies that transform society often fail to reward the investors who fund them.

quotes.text: Widespread attaching of "the four words" to bullish propositions suggests that the environment is being perceived as flawless.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo to Oaktree clients, "This Time It's Different"
quotes.source_title: This Time It's Different (Howard Marks memo)
quotes.gist: When everyone says "this time it's different" to justify bullishness, risk is being ignored.

quotes.text: The auto industry transformed the world, but many hundreds of car makes became road kill – among them the Berkshire and Omaha.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Fortune essay based on his Sun Valley remarks
quotes.source_title: Mr. Buffett on the Stock Market (Fortune, 1999)
quotes.gist: A technology can transform the world while most of the companies built on it die and their investors lose.

quotes.text: The worst sort of business is one that grows rapidly, requires significant capital to engender the growth, and then earns little or no money. Think airlines.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2007 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2007 Annual Letter
quotes.gist: Fast growth that demands huge capital and earns little is the worst business model, a warning for capital-hungry cyclical industries.

quotes.text: There is no doubt that investors are applying exuberance with regard to AI. The question is whether it’s irrational.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo to Oaktree clients, "Is It a Bubble?"
quotes.source_title: Is It a Bubble? (Howard Marks memo)
quotes.gist: Investors are clearly exuberant about AI; whether that exuberance is irrational is still open.

quotes.text: So AI might be a little overhyped now, but underhyped long term.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.role: Chairman and CEO, Duquesne Family Office
quotes.context: CNBC Squawk Box interview
quotes.source_title: Stanley Druckenmiller cut his Nvidia stake in late March, says AI may be a bit overhyped short term
quotes.gist: AI may be overhyped in the short run but underestimated over the long run, much like the internet.

quotes.text: That thought might be particularly seductive in these early days of the information revolution (which I wholeheartedly believe in).
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Fortune essay based on his Sun Valley remarks
quotes.source_title: Mr. Buffett on the Stock Market (Fortune, 1999)
quotes.gist: He believed in the technology revolution yet warned that betting on an industry's impact is a seductive trap for investors.

quotes.text: AI is real. AI in total will pay off, just like cars in total paid off, TV in total paid off
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: Interview remarks on AI and market risk, reported by Fortune
quotes.source_title: Markets look unstoppable, but JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon sees a 30% chance of a correction: 'I'm far more worried than others'
quotes.gist: AI will pay off overall, as cars and TV did, even if many individual investors in it do poorly.

quotes.text: These companies – the companies that are so highly valued – actually have earnings and stuff like that.
quotes.speaker: Jerome Powell
quotes.context: FOMC press conference
quotes.source_title: Powell gave traders a green light to double down on AI, but the markets punished Meta and Microsoft anyway (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Unlike dot-com firms, today's highly valued AI leaders have real earnings, so the boom is different.

quotes.text: There is not an AI bubble. There is the opposite.
quotes.speaker: Larry Fink
quotes.context: Milken Institute Global Conference, as reported by Business Insider
quotes.source_title: Larry Fink says there's the 'opposite' of an AI bubble, and the world isn't 'moving fast enough' on AI infrastructure (Moneywise via Yahoo Finance)
quotes.gist: AI is under-built, not a bubble; the world is not investing fast enough in AI infrastructure.

quotes.text: To ask whether AI is a bubble is a foolish question.
quotes.speaker: Masayoshi Son
quotes.context: SoftBank Group annual company event in Tokyo (AP report, translated)
quotes.source_title: 'Those who condemn AI are themselves spitting upward': SoftBank's CEO estimates $5 trillion needed annually to meet AI demand (AP via Fortune)
quotes.gist: AI will transform life profitably, so the bubble question itself is foolish.

quotes.text: We're going to see $10 to $12 trillion in revenue generation within the next five to ten years from almost nothing now.
quotes.speaker: Cathie Wood
quotes.role: Founder, CEO and CIO, ARK Invest
quotes.context: Bloomberg Television interview
quotes.source_title: Cathie Wood says AI already boosting labor productivity (Investing.com via Hellenic Shipping News)
quotes.gist: AI will create $10 to $12 trillion of new revenue within a decade, a huge productivity boom.

quotes.text: And once again there is a Cisco at the center of it all, with the picks and shovels for all and the expansive vision to go with it.
quotes.speaker: Michael Burry
quotes.role: Founder, Scion Asset Management; author, Cassandra Unchained
quotes.context: First post on his Substack, Cassandra Unchained
quotes.source_title: 'Big Short' investor Michael Burry warns Nvidia is the Cisco equivalent in today's AI boom (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Nvidia is today's Cisco, the picks-and-shovels darling of a bubble that ended in a crash.

quotes.text: If the economic life on these things [Nvidia's chips] is three years ... the whole economics of a lot of these deals kind of falls apart.
quotes.speaker: Jim Chanos
quotes.context: Yahoo Finance interview on GPU-backed debt
quotes.source_title: Famed short seller Jim Chanos sees risks in growing debt market backed by Nvidia's AI chips: 'There's going to be debt defaults'
quotes.gist: If Nvidia GPUs wear out in about three years, the economics of many GPU-financed data center deals collapse.

quotes.text: Everyone's excited, trying to get in at the same time, so there's double ordering, triple ordering, quadruple ordering, and then there is an inventory correction.
quotes.speaker: Cathie Wood
quotes.role: Founder, CEO and CIO, ARK Invest
quotes.context: Podcast interview with the WSJ's Dion Rabouin, reported by Business Insider
quotes.source_title: Cathie Wood says she's been selling Nvidia stock: 'It has become a check-the-box stock' (Business Insider)
quotes.gist: Nvidia is a very cyclical stock, and AI chip double-ordering will end in an inventory correction.

quotes.text: I don't like its location.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting, on selling TSMC
quotes.source_title: Warren Buffett is anxious about doing business in Taiwan, saying he would 'feel better' about dealings in Japan (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Even a marvelous chipmaker like TSMC carries geopolitical risk from its Taiwan location.

quotes.text: And then it turns out that the old rules do still apply, and the cycle resumes. In the end, trees don't grow to the sky, and few things go to zero.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo to Oaktree clients, "You Can't Predict. You Can Prepare."
quotes.source_title: You Can't Predict. You Can Prepare. (Howard Marks memo)
quotes.gist: Booms that seem to break the rules eventually revert as the cycle reasserts itself.

quotes.text: Rather, most phenomena turn out to be cyclical.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo to Oaktree clients, "You Can't Predict. You Can Prepare."
quotes.source_title: You Can't Predict. You Can Prepare. (Howard Marks memo)
quotes.gist: Trends rarely run in a straight line; most things prove cyclical.

quotes.text: There could be 2-3x more upside in Nvidia if it follows Cisco's valuation path to its peak.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Siegel
quotes.role: Professor emeritus, Wharton; senior economist, WisdomTree
quotes.context: Remarks reported by Business Insider
quotes.source_title: Nvidia could be worth $6 trillion if it follows Cisco's dot-com trajectory, says Jeremy Siegel
quotes.gist: Nvidia could still multiply if it follows Cisco's path, but that path ended at a bubble peak.

quotes.text: The beginnings of a speculative bubble may be forming but it is impossible to tell when it will end.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Siegel
quotes.role: Professor emeritus, Wharton; senior economist, WisdomTree
quotes.context: Weekly WisdomTree commentary
quotes.source_title: AI Stocks Including Nvidia Face Bubble Risks, Warns 'Wizard of Wharton': 'Impossible To Tell When It Will End' (Benzinga)
quotes.gist: AI chip stocks may be entering a speculative bubble, but its end cannot be timed.

quotes.text: We've had a hell of a run. A lot of what we recognized has become recognized by the marketplace now.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.role: Chairman and CEO, Duquesne Family Office
quotes.context: CNBC Squawk Box interview, on cutting his Nvidia stake
quotes.source_title: Stanley Druckenmiller cut his Nvidia stake in late March, says AI may be a bit overhyped short term
quotes.gist: After a huge Nvidia gain, the market has caught up to his thesis, so he trimmed without turning bearish.

quotes.text: This cyclical market has historically exhibited both demand and price volatility, but we believe it is in the early innings of de-commoditization.
quotes.speaker: Dan Loeb
quotes.context: Third Point Q3 2025 investor letter, on memory chips and SK Hynix
quotes.source_title: Third Point Q3 2025 Investor Letter (Hedge Fund Alpha)
quotes.gist: AI demand may be turning the boom-bust memory chip market into a less cyclical, de-commoditized business.

quotes.text: I've made so many mistakes in my investment career; one of them was I sold all my Nvidia, probably somewhere between $800 and $950.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.role: Chairman and CEO, Duquesne Family Office
quotes.context: Bloomberg interview with Sonali Basak
quotes.source_title: Billionaire investor is licking his wounds after selling Nvidia (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Selling Nvidia too early was a mistake because the stock kept compounding.

quotes.text: I respect Jensen, I respect Nvidia so much, I don't want to sell a single share.
quotes.speaker: Masayoshi Son
quotes.context: FII Priority Asia forum, Tokyo
quotes.source_title: 'I don't want to sell a single share': SoftBank boss Masayoshi Son says he was crying over dumping Nvidia stock (Business Insider via Yahoo Finance)
quotes.gist: He sold Nvidia only to fund other AI bets and would hold every share if he could.

quotes.text: I think Nvidia will be the first $10 trillion company.
quotes.speaker: Brad Gerstner
quotes.context: CNBC Halftime Report interview at the Milken Conference, reported by Benzinga
quotes.source_title: Nvidia Will Become First $10 Trillion Company, Says Altimeter CEO Brad Gerstner (Benzinga via Longport)
quotes.gist: Nvidia will keep compounding to become the first $10 trillion company.

quotes.text: Tesla's market capitalization is ridiculously overvalued today and has been for a good long time.
quotes.speaker: Michael Burry
quotes.role: Founder, Scion Asset Management; author, Cassandra Unchained
quotes.context: Substack post
quotes.source_title: 'Big Short' investor Michael Burry calls Tesla stock 'ridiculously overvalued' and warns on Musk's pay plan (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Tesla's valuation is absurdly high and has been for years.

quotes.text: This is the anti-Amazon.
quotes.speaker: Jim Chanos
quotes.context: CNBC Institutional Investor Delivering Alpha conference
quotes.source_title: Hedge Fund Manager Who Spotted Fraud at Enron Calls Tesla 'The Anti-Amazon' (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Tesla is not a capital-light compounder like Amazon but a cash-burning business valued as if it were.

quotes.text: And when you need that amount of money just to run your business model, you put yourself at risk.
quotes.speaker: Jim Chanos
quotes.context: CNBC Institutional Investor Delivering Alpha conference
quotes.source_title: Hedge Fund Manager Who Spotted Fraud at Enron Calls Tesla 'The Anti-Amazon' (Fortune)
quotes.gist: A company that constantly needs outside capital to function, like Tesla then, is fragile.

quotes.text: In bubbles, investors treat the leading companies – and pay for their stocks – as though the firms are sure to remain leaders for decades.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo to Oaktree clients, "On Bubble Watch"
quotes.source_title: On Bubble Watch (Howard Marks memo)
quotes.gist: Bubbles price today's leaders as permanent winners, which history rarely bears out.

quotes.text: When risk/reward becomes disconnected, we step back – even if it means temporary underperformance.
quotes.speaker: David Einhorn
quotes.context: Greenlight Capital Q3 2025 investor letter, on the Magnificent Seven and AI spending
quotes.source_title: Greenlight Capital's Einhorn Opts Out of AI Frenzy: "The Math Doesn't Add Up" (Tiger Newspress)
quotes.gist: He avoids the mega-cap AI trade because its risk/reward no longer adds up, even at the cost of lagging.

quotes.text: The day after Chat came out, the Mag Seven lifted the market on its broad shoulders and staggered forward.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Grantham
quotes.role: Co-founder and long-term investment strategist, GMO
quotes.context: Interview with Fortune
quotes.source_title: Legendary investor says the AI boom masks a deeper crisis (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Since ChatGPT the market has leaned on a handful of mega-caps, a fragile bubble within a bubble.

quotes.text: It remains to be seen whether gains become more broad-based or remain concentrated and thus higher risk as we approach year end.
quotes.speaker: Dan Loeb
quotes.context: Third Point Q3 2025 investor letter
quotes.source_title: Third Point Q3 2025 Investor Letter (Hedge Fund Alpha)
quotes.gist: Narrow, concentrated gains are riskier, and it is unclear whether the rally will broaden.

quotes.text: ... Tesla's stock movements caused increased variability in the entire portfolio.
quotes.speaker: Ron Baron and Michael Baron
quotes.role: Portfolio managers, Baron Partners Fund (Baron Capital)
quotes.context: Baron Partners Fund Q4 2025 shareholder letter, on trimming Tesla
quotes.source_title: Quarterly Letter: Baron Partners Fund Q4 2025
quotes.gist: Even a committed Tesla bull trimmed because one huge position made the whole fund swing.

quotes.text: Today's S&P-leading companies are, in many ways, much better than the best companies of the past. They enjoy massive technological advantages.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo to Oaktree clients, "On Bubble Watch"
quotes.source_title: On Bubble Watch (Howard Marks memo)
quotes.gist: Today's mega-cap leaders are higher quality than past market leaders such as the Nifty Fifty.

quotes.text: I'm somewhat embarrassed to say that Tim Cook has made Berkshire a lot more money than I've ever made [for] Berkshire Hathaway.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting
quotes.source_title: Warren Buffett credits Apple CEO Tim Cook with making 'a lot more money than I've ever made' for Berkshire Hathaway (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Berkshire's concentrated Apple stake earned more than Buffett's own decisions, showing the payoff of owning a mega-cap winner.

quotes.text: Over time, it takes just a few winners to work wonders.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2022 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2022 Annual Letter
quotes.gist: A handful of big winners drive most long-term returns.

quotes.text: The lesson for investors: The weeds wither away in significance as the flowers bloom.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2022 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2022 Annual Letter
quotes.gist: Over time the winners grow to dominate a portfolio while the losers fade in importance.

quotes.text: Autonomous taxi networks represent the biggest AI project in the world.
quotes.speaker: Cathie Wood
quotes.role: Founder, CEO and CIO, ARK Invest
quotes.context: Remarks on Tesla reported by Fortune
quotes.source_title: Tesla bull Cathie Wood says it isn't just Elon Musk's politics that are causing Tesla's 'demand hit.' It's also a bad economy (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Robotaxis, Tesla's core bull case, are the largest AI opportunity in the world.

quotes.text: ARK's updated open-source Tesla model yields an expected value of $2,600 per share in 2029.
quotes.speaker: ARK Invest research team (Tasha Keeney, Sam Korus, Daniel Maguire)
quotes.context: ARK published Tesla valuation model
quotes.source_title: ARK's Tesla Price Target 2029 (ARK Invest)
quotes.gist: ARK's model values Tesla at $2,600 a share by 2029, mostly on robotaxis.

quotes.text: We are extremely confident in the company's prospects and ability to become a significantly more valuable business.
quotes.speaker: Ron Baron and Michael Baron
quotes.role: Portfolio managers, Baron Partners Fund (Baron Capital)
quotes.context: Baron Partners Fund Q4 2025 shareholder letter, on Tesla
quotes.source_title: Quarterly Letter: Baron Partners Fund Q4 2025
quotes.gist: Tesla will become a far more valuable company, so it remains a top holding.

quotes.text: For the first 10 years of this bull market, which is the longest in history, we lacked such wild speculation. But now we have it. In record amounts.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Grantham
quotes.role: Co-founder and long-term investment strategist, GMO
quotes.context: GMO viewpoint, "Waiting for the Last Dance"
quotes.source_title: Waiting for the Last Dance (GMO)
quotes.gist: Retail-fueled speculation reached record extremes, the hallmark of a bubble's final phase.

quotes.text: Each cycle is different and unique – but every historical parallel suggests that the worst is yet to come.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Grantham
quotes.role: Co-founder and long-term investment strategist, GMO
quotes.context: GMO viewpoint, "Entering the Superbubble's Final Act"
quotes.source_title: Entering the Superbubble's Final Act (GMO)
quotes.gist: Every past superbubble ended in deep losses, so the worst of the unwind lies ahead.

quotes.text: For whatever reasons, markets now exhibit far more casino-like behavior than they did when I was young.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2023 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2023 Annual Letter
quotes.gist: Today's markets behave more like a casino than in the past.

quotes.text: When the capital development of a country becomes a by-product of the activities of a casino, the job is likely to be ill-done.
quotes.speaker: John Maynard Keynes
quotes.role: Economist; bursar and investment manager, King's College, Cambridge
quotes.context: The General Theory, Chapter 12
quotes.source_title: The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money, Chapter 12
quotes.gist: When speculation drives capital allocation, an economy invests badly.

quotes.text: If I have one message for those listening who are buying memecoins: buyer beware.
quotes.speaker: Cathie Wood
quotes.role: Founder, CEO and CIO, ARK Invest
quotes.context: Bloomberg Television interview, reported by Fortune
quotes.source_title: Cathie Wood says most memecoins will end up 'worthless' (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Most memecoins will end up worthless, so speculators should beware.

quotes.text: Those who merely look on feel incredible envy and regret and – motivated by the fear of continuing to miss out – pile in.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo to Oaktree clients, "Is It a Bubble?"
quotes.source_title: Is It a Bubble? (Howard Marks memo)
quotes.gist: FOMO pulls bystanders into a mania late, which is how bubbles inflate.

quotes.text: Investors in stocks these days are expecting far too much, and I'm going to explain why.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Fortune essay based on his Sun Valley remarks
quotes.source_title: Mr. Buffett on the Stock Market (Fortune, 1999)
quotes.gist: At the height of the dot-com mania, investors expected returns far beyond what was achievable.

quotes.text: In the short run the market acts as a voting machine; in the long run it becomes a weighing machine.
quotes.speaker: Benjamin Graham (as quoted by Warren Buffett)
quotes.context: Quoted by Buffett ("As Ben Graham taught me") in the 2023 Berkshire letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2023 Annual Letter
quotes.gist: Popularity drives prices for a while, but fundamentals win in the end.

quotes.text: Speculators may do no harm as bubbles on a steady stream of enterprise. But the position is serious when enterprise becomes the bubble on a whirlpool of speculation.
quotes.speaker: John Maynard Keynes
quotes.role: Economist; bursar and investment manager, King's College, Cambridge
quotes.context: The General Theory, Chapter 12
quotes.source_title: The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money, Chapter 12
quotes.gist: Some speculation is harmless; the danger comes when speculation dominates enterprise.

quotes.text: But how do we know when irrational exuberance has unduly escalated asset values, which then become subject to unexpected and prolonged contractions as they have in Japan over the past decade?
quotes.speaker: Alan Greenspan
quotes.context: Francis Boyer Lecture, American Enterprise Institute
quotes.source_title: The Challenge of Central Banking in a Democratic Society (Federal Reserve)
quotes.gist: Exuberance can inflate prices into a painful bust, yet spotting it in real time is hard.

quotes.text: If anything, now is so much more potentially explosive than 1999.
quotes.speaker: Paul Tudor Jones
quotes.role: Founder and CIO, Tudor Investment Corp.
quotes.context: CNBC interview
quotes.source_title: Billionaire Paul Tudor Jones Sees a Surge Ahead in the Stock Market. Should You Run to Buy AI Stocks?
quotes.gist: Conditions today are even more combustible than 1999, for both a melt-up and the bust that follows.

quotes.text: Now we emphatically do not have 1999-2000 levels of speculation in the markets or tech.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Siegel
quotes.role: Professor emeritus, Wharton; senior economist, WisdomTree
quotes.context: Remarks reported by Business Insider
quotes.source_title: Nvidia could be worth $6 trillion if it follows Cisco's dot-com trajectory, says Jeremy Siegel
quotes.gist: Current speculation is nowhere near dot-com levels, so the rally has room.

quotes.text: Bull markets could go on a lot longer than you think.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: Interview remarks reported by Fortune
quotes.source_title: Markets look unstoppable, but JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon sees a 30% chance of a correction: 'I'm far more worried than others'
quotes.gist: Even a frothy bull market can run much longer than skeptics expect.

quotes.text: Don’t sell just because there’s a bubble.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: CNBC interview
quotes.source_title: 'Don't sell just because there's a bubble,' says Ray Dalio, but be prepared for low returns over the next 10 years (Fortune)
quotes.gist: A bubble alone is not a sell signal; it pops only when something pricks it.

quotes.text: Folly makes money. Creative destruction and manic folly are exactly why the U.S. is the center of innovation in the world.
quotes.speaker: Michael Burry
quotes.role: Founder, Scion Asset Management; author, Cassandra Unchained
quotes.context: First post on his Substack, Cassandra Unchained
quotes.source_title: 'Big Short' investor Michael Burry warns Nvidia is the Cisco equivalent in today's AI boom (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Even a famous bear concedes that manic speculation funds the innovation that makes the U.S. lead.

quotes.text: My guess is that I think all the ingredients are in place for some blow off.
quotes.speaker: Paul Tudor Jones
quotes.role: Founder and CIO, Tudor Investment Corp.
quotes.context: CNBC interview
quotes.source_title: Billionaire Paul Tudor Jones Sees a Surge Ahead in the Stock Market. Should You Run to Buy AI Stocks?
quotes.gist: Conditions favor a speculative blow-off rally like 1999 before any top.

quotes.text: Today in the U.S. we are in the fourth superbubble of the last hundred years.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Grantham
quotes.role: Co-founder and Long-Term Investment Strategist, GMO
quotes.context: GMO viewpoint 'Let the Wild Rumpus Begin'
quotes.source_title: Let the Wild Rumpus Begin | GMO
quotes.gist: Grantham judged US stocks to be in a once-in-a-generation superbubble.

quotes.text: much less dangerous to own and will very likely over five or 10 years crush the U.S. market as has happened several times.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Grantham
quotes.role: Co-founder and Long-Term Investment Strategist, GMO
quotes.context: Bloomberg podcast interview, reported by MarketWatch; words refer to non-US markets
quotes.source_title: Jeremy Grantham on the meltdown coming for U.S. stocks and where he's putting his money now (MarketWatch via Tiger Brokers)
quotes.gist: Grantham expects cheaper non-US markets to far outperform an overvalued US market over the next five to ten years.

quotes.text: In that 27-year period, when people bought the S&P at p/e ratios in line with today's multiple of 22, they always earned ten-year returns between plus 2% and minus 2%.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo 'On Bubble Watch'
quotes.source_title: On Bubble Watch | Oaktree Capital
quotes.gist: Historically, buying the S&P 500 at today's forward P/E has produced roughly flat ten-year returns.

quotes.text: There is definitely a bubble in markets.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: CNBC interview, reported by Dow Jones
quotes.source_title: "There's Definitely a Bubble in Markets," Ray Dalio Says. But That Doesn't Mean You Should Sell
quotes.gist: Dalio says markets are in a bubble, though he does not argue it is about to pop.

quotes.text: Obviously the AI boom that is now in the early stages of a bubble had a big effect on everything.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: 2025 retrospective post on X, reported by Fortune
quotes.source_title: Ray Dalio says AI is in the early stages of a bubble, so watch out for 2026 | Fortune
quotes.gist: Dalio sees the AI boom as an early-stage bubble that drove 2025 market returns.

quotes.text: But how do we know when irrational exuberance has unduly escalated asset values, which then become subject to unexpected and prolonged contractions as they have in Japan over the past decade?
quotes.speaker: Alan Greenspan
quotes.context: Francis Boyer Lecture, American Enterprise Institute
quotes.source_title: FRB: Speech, Greenspan, The challenge of central banking in a democratic society, December 5, 1996
quotes.gist: Greenspan warned that euphoric markets can inflate asset prices that later suffer long declines.

quotes.text: the markets, while high-priced and perhaps frothy, don't seem nutty to me.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo 'On Bubble Watch'
quotes.source_title: On Bubble Watch | Oaktree Capital
quotes.gist: Marks sees US stocks as expensive and somewhat frothy but not irrational.

quotes.text: That's typically a good setup for value investors. It hasn't paid off yet, but we're not in bubble territory.
quotes.speaker: Cliff Asness
quotes.role: Co-founder and CIO, AQR Capital Management
quotes.context: Bloomberg Television interview, reported by Hedgeweek
quotes.source_title: US stocks expensive but not in bubble territory, says AQR boss | Hedgeweek
quotes.gist: Asness says investors are overpaying for favored stocks, which favors value, but the market is not a bubble.

quotes.text: Long ago, Ben Graham taught me that "Price is what you pay; value is what you get."
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2008 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2008 Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: What matters is the gap between the price paid and the underlying value received.

quotes.text: Almost all the bubble is in the Information Technology and Communication Services sectors.
quotes.speaker: Ed Yardeni
quotes.context: Yardeni Research commentary, reported by Benzinga
quotes.source_title: Are The Roaring 2020s Still Alive? Yardeni Says 2026 Could Surprise Everyone (Benzinga via Webull)
quotes.gist: Yardeni sees the froth concentrated in tech and communication stocks rather than the whole market.

quotes.text: While I don't think we're in a bubble yet, I think investors should be looking for broader participation in the markets.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Siegel
quotes.role: Wharton professor emeritus; Senior Economist, WisdomTree
quotes.context: Weekly WisdomTree commentary, reported by Fortune
quotes.source_title: Are we in a market bubble? Jeremy Siegel weighs in | Fortune
quotes.gist: Siegel rejects the bubble label for the AI rally and expects gains to broaden beyond megacaps.

quotes.text: There is no long-run advantage of bonds over stocks at these valuations or circumstances.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Siegel
quotes.role: Wharton professor emeritus; Senior Economist, WisdomTree
quotes.context: Betterment webinar 'Making Sense of Today's Markets'
quotes.source_title: Why the market's 'doom' signals are wrong, says Jeremy J. Siegel | Betterment
quotes.gist: Even at current valuations, Siegel argues stocks remain the better long-run holding than bonds.

quotes.text: Despite what some commentators currently view as an extraordinary cash position at Berkshire, the great majority of your money remains in equities.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2024 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2024 Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: Buffett pushes back on reading Berkshire's cash pile as a bearish market call.

quotes.text: Equities will almost certainly outperform cash over the next decade, probably by a substantial degree.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: New York Times op-ed 'Buy American. I Am.'
quotes.source_title: "Buy American. I Am." Ten Years Later | Crossing Wall Street
quotes.gist: At crisis-era prices, Buffett judged stocks very likely to beat cash by a wide margin over ten years.

quotes.text: Let's split the difference and aim for 10,000 by the end of the Roaring 2020s.
quotes.speaker: Ed Yardeni
quotes.context: Yardeni Research commentary, reported by Benzinga
quotes.source_title: Are The Roaring 2020s Still Alive? Yardeni Says 2026 Could Surprise Everyone (Benzinga via Webull)
quotes.gist: Yardeni targets the S&P 500 at 10,000 by 2030 on a productivity-led boom.

quotes.text: The checklist for a superbubble running through its phases is now complete and the wild rumpus can begin at any time.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Grantham
quotes.role: Co-founder and Long-Term Investment Strategist, GMO
quotes.context: GMO viewpoint 'Let the Wild Rumpus Begin'
quotes.source_title: Let the Wild Rumpus Begin | GMO
quotes.gist: Grantham warned that every precondition for a bubble's collapse was in place and a crash could start anytime.

quotes.text: everyone built too many railroads, and everyone lost their money. That will happen in AI.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Grantham
quotes.role: Co-founder and Long-Term Investment Strategist, GMO
quotes.context: MoneyWeek Talks podcast
quotes.source_title: Jeremy Grantham: How to invest like a stock market legend | MoneyWeek
quotes.gist: Grantham predicts AI investors will lose money the way railroad investors did after overbuilding.

quotes.text: You're going to have unbelievable opportunities in the next couple of years.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.role: Chairman and CEO, Duquesne Family Office
quotes.context: Sohn Investment Conference
quotes.source_title: How bad will the recession be? Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller on a hard landing | Fortune
quotes.gist: Druckenmiller advised preserving capital because he expected much cheaper prices ahead.

quotes.text: You have to be able to withstand shocks unexpectedly arriving, and to do that, you need little or no debt
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Grantham
quotes.role: Co-founder and Long-Term Investment Strategist, GMO
quotes.context: Bloomberg podcast interview, reported by MarketWatch
quotes.source_title: Jeremy Grantham on the meltdown coming for U.S. stocks and where he's putting his money now (MarketWatch via Tiger Brokers)
quotes.gist: Grantham urges investors to avoid leverage so they can survive sudden market shocks.

quotes.text: That doesn't mean we can't fall another 20% from here, too.
quotes.speaker: Larry Fink
quotes.context: Economic Club of New York
quotes.source_title: BlackRock's Fink says CEOs tell him they think US economy is in a recession | Fox Business
quotes.gist: Even while calling the tariff selloff a long-run buying opportunity, Fink warned of a further 20% drop.

quotes.text: Since no one can say definitively whether this is a bubble, I'd advise that no one should go all-in without acknowledging that they face the risk of ruin if things go badly.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo 'Is It a Bubble?'
quotes.source_title: Is It a Bubble? | Oaktree Capital
quotes.gist: Marks recommends a moderate position on AI: neither all-in nor all-out.

quotes.text: I want to reiterate, a lot can go up before the bubble bursts.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: CNBC interview, reported by Dow Jones
quotes.source_title: "There's Definitely a Bubble in Markets," Ray Dalio Says. But That Doesn't Mean You Should Sell
quotes.gist: Dalio says a bubble can keep inflating for a long time, so it is not by itself a sell signal.

quotes.text: No one can tell you when these will happen. The light can at any time go from green to red without pausing at yellow.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2017 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2017 Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: Big declines will come without warning, so nobody can time them.

quotes.text: A simple rule dictates my buying: Be fearful when others are greedy, and be greedy when others are fearful.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: New York Times op-ed 'Buy American. I Am.'
quotes.source_title: "Buy American. I Am." Ten Years Later | Crossing Wall Street
quotes.gist: Buy when the crowd panics and be cautious when it is euphoric.

quotes.text: Time is on your side in the stock market.
quotes.speaker: Peter Lynch
quotes.context: PBS Frontline interview
quotes.source_title: Interview with Peter Lynch | Betting on the Market | FRONTLINE | PBS
quotes.gist: Long holding periods, not timing, are what reward stock investors.

quotes.text: If it makes a difference to you whether your stocks are down 15% or not, you need to get a somewhat different investment philosophy.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting
quotes.source_title: Buffett downplays recent market volatility as 'really nothing,' saying it's part of investing (CNBC via NBC Miami)
quotes.gist: Investors who cannot tolerate a 15% drop should not be reacting to it; they need a different approach.

quotes.text: Berkshire will never prefer ownership of cash-equivalent assets over the ownership of good businesses, whether controlled or only partially owned.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2024 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2024 Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: Despite a record cash pile, Buffett says Berkshire prefers owning businesses to sitting in cash.

quotes.text: In short, bad news is an investor's best friend.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: New York Times op-ed 'Buy American. I Am.'
quotes.source_title: "Buy American. I Am." Ten Years Later | Crossing Wall Street
quotes.gist: Crises create the cheapest prices, so long-term investors should welcome them.

quotes.text: Far more money has been lost by investors preparing for corrections, or trying to anticipate corrections, than has been lost in corrections themselves.
quotes.speaker: Peter Lynch
quotes.context: Widely cited Lynch maxim; original venue not confirmed
quotes.source_title: Peter Lynch on Stock Market Losses | A Wealth of Common Sense
quotes.gist: Trying to sidestep corrections costs investors more than the corrections do.

quotes.text: Let's say Berkshire went down 50% next week, I would regard that as a fantastic opportunity, and it wouldn't bother me in the least.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting
quotes.source_title: Buffett downplays recent market volatility as 'really nothing,' saying it's part of investing (CNBC via NBC Miami)
quotes.gist: A 50% crash would be a buying opportunity, not a cause for worry.

quotes.text: I think the risk is now of a substantial leg up rally from here.
quotes.speaker: Tom Lee
quotes.role: Co-founder and Head of Research, Fundstrat Global Advisors
quotes.context: CNBC interview, reported by Benzinga
quotes.source_title: Tom Lee says V-shaped rally among most hated ever as market nears all-time highs, warns of possible 'face-ripper' surge | Benzinga
quotes.gist: With investors still cautious after the tariff selloff, Lee saw the bigger risk as missing a strong rally.

quotes.text: That hurricane is right out there down the road coming our way.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: Bernstein Strategic Decisions Conference
quotes.source_title: Jamie Dimon is warning that an economic 'hurricane' is on the way: 'You better brace yourself' (CNBC via ABC7)
quotes.gist: Dimon warned of an economic hurricane from Fed tightening and the war in Ukraine.

quotes.text: And I'm worried about something worse than a recession if this isn't handled well.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: NBC 'Meet the Press'
quotes.source_title: Billionaire hedge fund manager warns tariffs could trigger conditions 'worse than a recession' | FOX 11 Los Angeles
quotes.gist: Dalio said tariffs and debt could push the US into something worse than an ordinary recession.

quotes.text: The far more critical consideration is the coming contraction in global economic activity.
quotes.speaker: Van R. Hoisington and Lacy H. Hunt
quotes.role: President and Chief Economist, Hoisington Investment Management
quotes.context: Quarterly Review and Outlook, Second Quarter 2025
quotes.source_title: Hoisington Investment Management Quarterly Review and Outlook, Second Quarter 2025
quotes.gist: The Hoisington team expected a global economic contraction to be the dominant force ahead.

quotes.text: It's pretty clear that we have the look of soon to be at the front end of a recession.
quotes.speaker: Jeffrey Gundlach
quotes.context: DoubleLine investor webcast
quotes.source_title: Billionaire investor Stanley Druckenmiller and 'bond king' Jeffrey Gundlach issue recession warning | Fortune
quotes.gist: Gundlach read the 2023 data as signaling an imminent recession.

quotes.text: I think that's probably a likely outcome.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: Fox Business 'Mornings with Maria', asked if a recession was coming
quotes.source_title: Jamie Dimon: Recession a 'Likely Outcome' of US Tariffs | PYMNTS
quotes.gist: Asked about recession after the tariff shock, Dimon said it was probably the likely outcome.

quotes.text: I don't think [a U.S. recession] is inevitable because the structure of the economy is so strong, but the risk has become uncomfortably high.
quotes.speaker: Mohamed El-Erian
quotes.context: CNBC interview at the Ambrosetti Forum, Cernobbio
quotes.source_title: El-Erian says U.S. recession risks are now 'uncomfortably high' (CNBC via NBC San Diego)
quotes.gist: El-Erian saw recession odds near 50% after tariffs, though not inevitable given a strong economy.

quotes.text: Most CEOs I talk to would say we are probably in a recession right now.
quotes.speaker: Larry Fink
quotes.context: Economic Club of New York
quotes.source_title: BlackRock's Fink says CEOs tell him they think US economy is in a recession | Fox Business
quotes.gist: Fink reported that most CEOs he spoke with believed the US was already in recession.

quotes.text: There's a lot of recessionary signals out there.
quotes.speaker: Jeffrey Gundlach
quotes.context: Webinar hosted by Rosenberg Research, reported by Reuters
quotes.source_title: DoubleLine CEO expects imminent US recession, government debt surge (Reuters via The Wealth Advisor)
quotes.gist: Gundlach saw multiple indicators pointing toward a US recession.

quotes.text: it's just naive not to be open-minded to something really, really bad happening.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.role: Chairman and CEO, Duquesne Family Office
quotes.context: Sohn Investment Conference
quotes.source_title: How bad will the recession be? Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller on a hard landing | Fortune
quotes.gist: Druckenmiller expected a hard landing and said investors should be open to a very bad outcome.

quotes.text: I've always said if you spend 13 minutes a year on economics, you've wasted 10 minutes.
quotes.speaker: Peter Lynch
quotes.context: PBS Frontline interview
quotes.source_title: Interview with Peter Lynch | Betting on the Market | FRONTLINE | PBS
quotes.gist: Economic forecasting is mostly a waste of an investor's time.

quotes.text: I deal in facts, not forecasting the future. That's crystal ball stuff. That doesn't work.
quotes.speaker: Peter Lynch
quotes.context: PBS Frontline interview
quotes.source_title: Interview with Peter Lynch | Betting on the Market | FRONTLINE | PBS
quotes.gist: Lynch rejects predicting the economy and focuses on company facts.

quotes.text: The economy is strong overall and has made significant progress toward our goals over the past two years.
quotes.speaker: Jerome Powell
quotes.context: FOMC press conference
quotes.source_title: Transcript of Chair Powell's Press Conference, March 19, 2025
quotes.gist: Powell described the US economy as strong despite rising tariff uncertainty.

quotes.text: We see the consumer continue to be solid, and that should bode well for the economy.
quotes.speaker: Brian Moynihan
quotes.role: Chairman and CEO, Bank of America
quotes.context: CNBC 'Squawk Box' interview
quotes.source_title: Bank of America's CEO says economic growth is better than people think and the Fed should stay on hold (CNBC via NBC Chicago)
quotes.gist: Moynihan said customer spending data showed a solid consumer supporting growth.

quotes.text: I think instead of a recession unfolding, the economy is actually slipping into an expansion.
quotes.speaker: Tom Lee
quotes.role: Co-founder and Head of Research, Fundstrat Global Advisors
quotes.context: CNBC interview, reported by Fortune
quotes.source_title: Wall Street's biggest bull called this year's stock market rally, now instead of a recession he says... (Fortune via The Wealth Advisor)
quotes.gist: Against the 2023 consensus, Lee argued the economy was entering an expansion, not a recession.

quotes.text: Our unwavering conclusion: Never bet against America.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2020 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2020 Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: Over the long run the US economy has always prevailed, so betting against it is a mistake.

quotes.text: And bonds are not the place to be these days.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2020 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2020 Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: With the 10-year near 1%, Buffett called bonds a poor place for investors' money.

quotes.text: It is hard to imagine how the market absorbs such a large increase in supply without materially higher rates.
quotes.speaker: Bill Ackman
quotes.context: Post on X explaining his 30-year Treasury short, reported by Benzinga
quotes.source_title: Hedge Fund Guru Bill Ackman Bets Against US Treasuries, Expects 30-Year Yields To Surge To 5.5% | Benzinga
quotes.gist: Ackman shorted 30-year Treasuries, arguing heavy issuance would force long yields much higher.

quotes.text: You're going to see a crack in the bond market.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: Remarks at the Reagan forum in Simi Valley, reported by Benzinga
quotes.source_title: Jamie Dimon warns of bond market crisis caused by US debt binge: 'You're going to panic' | Benzinga
quotes.gist: Dimon predicted that US deficits and debt will eventually trigger a bond market break.

quotes.text: I worry that the federal government might be forced to restructure the Treasury debt.
quotes.speaker: Jeffrey Gundlach
quotes.context: Webinar hosted by Rosenberg Research, reported by Reuters
quotes.source_title: DoubleLine CEO expects imminent US recession, government debt surge (Reuters via The Wealth Advisor)
quotes.gist: Gundlach raised the risk that soaring federal debt could eventually force a Treasury restructuring.

quotes.text: Fixed-coupon bonds provide no protection against runaway currency.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2024 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2024 Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: Bonds fail as a hedge if fiscal folly debases the currency.

quotes.text: I made a lot of money this year betting on bonds going down because of the debt and had nothing do with the economy.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.role: Chairman and CEO, Duquesne Family Office
quotes.context: CNBC 'Squawk Box' interview transcript
quotes.source_title: CNBC Exclusive: CNBC Transcript: Duquesne Family Office Chair & CEO Stanley Druckenmiller Speaks with CNBC's "Squawk Box" Today
quotes.gist: Druckenmiller profited from shorting bonds on the view that US debt levels push yields up.

quotes.text: We're gonna be broke really quickly unless we get serious about dealing with our spending issues.
quotes.speaker: Paul Tudor Jones
quotes.role: Founder and CIO, Tudor Investment Corporation
quotes.context: Robin Hood Investors Conference sidelines, New York
quotes.source_title: Hedge Fund Alpha article on Paul Tudor Jones at the 2024 Robin Hood Investors Conference
quotes.gist: Tudor Jones, who said he would own no fixed income, warned US deficit spending is unsustainable.

quotes.text: My opinion is we're going to have 10-year rates at least at 5% or higher because of this embedded inflation.
quotes.speaker: Larry Fink
quotes.context: Berlin Global Dialogue, conversation with Bloomberg
quotes.source_title: Larry Fink sees 10-year Treasury yield at 5% due to embedded inflation | Fortune
quotes.gist: Fink expected structural inflation to keep 10-year yields at or above 5%.

quotes.text: On bonds. Invest in the curve. Various combinations 2/10, 2/5. Should go positive before year end.
quotes.speaker: Bill Gross
quotes.context: Post on X, embedded in Fortune
quotes.source_title: 'Bond king' Bill Gross predicts a recession in Q4 | Fortune
quotes.gist: Gross favored yield-curve steepeners, betting short rates fall relative to long rates rather than a simple long-bond call.

quotes.text: Once they move above 2%, the Fed is going to find a blip showing up on their radar screen and they will start thinking about how high do they want rates to go.
quotes.speaker: Jeffrey Gundlach
quotes.context: DoubleLine webcast
quotes.source_title: Rising rates may lead to Fed yield-curve control, Gundlach says | InvestmentNews
quotes.gist: Gundlach expected rising long yields to prompt the Fed to cap them through yield-curve control.

quotes.text: There is too much risk in the world to remain short bonds at current long-term rates.
quotes.speaker: Bill Ackman
quotes.context: Post on X announcing he covered his Treasury short
quotes.source_title: Bill Ackman says he covered his bond short | investingLive
quotes.gist: With 30-year yields near 5%, Ackman judged long bonds a useful hedge and closed his short.

quotes.text: We have more Treasuries now in our strategies than we've ever had.
quotes.speaker: Jeffrey Gundlach
quotes.context: Webinar hosted by Rosenberg Research, reported by Reuters
quotes.source_title: DoubleLine CEO expects imminent US recession, government debt surge (Reuters via The Wealth Advisor)
quotes.gist: Expecting recession, Gundlach loaded DoubleLine portfolios with a record share of Treasuries.

quotes.text: "Higher for longer" is yesterday's mantra.
quotes.speaker: Bill Gross
quotes.context: Post on X, embedded in Fortune
quotes.source_title: 'Bond king' Bill Gross predicts a recession in Q4 | Fortune
quotes.gist: Gross argued that the peak-rates narrative was ending and yields would come down.

quotes.text: Accordingly, we believe the outlook for long term Treasury bond yields to decline appears increasingly likely.
quotes.speaker: Van R. Hoisington and Lacy H. Hunt
quotes.role: President and Chief Economist, Hoisington Investment Management
quotes.context: Quarterly Review and Outlook, Fourth Quarter 2025
quotes.source_title: Hoisington Investment Management Quarterly Review and Outlook, Fourth Quarter 2025
quotes.gist: Easing labor costs and inflation make falling long Treasury yields increasingly likely.

quotes.text: This environment is very attractive for long horizon investors in long-term Treasury bonds.
quotes.speaker: Van R. Hoisington and Lacy H. Hunt
quotes.role: President and Chief Economist, Hoisington Investment Management
quotes.context: Quarterly Review and Outlook, Second Quarter 2025
quotes.source_title: Hoisington Investment Management Quarterly Review and Outlook, Second Quarter 2025
quotes.gist: A coming global contraction makes long Treasuries a strong buy for patient investors.

quotes.text: R* and inflationary expectations suggest the rally in long Treasury bonds will continue through 2024, with the strong prospect for an even longer horizon for this trend.
quotes.speaker: Hoisington Investment Management
quotes.role: Quarterly Review and Outlook (firm publication; Van Hoisington and Lacy Hunt's team)
quotes.context: Quarterly Review and Outlook, Fourth Quarter 2023
quotes.source_title: Hoisington Investment Management Quarterly Review and Outlook, Fourth Quarter 2023
quotes.gist: Low neutral rates and falling inflation expectations point to a multi-year rally in long Treasuries.

quotes.text: Don't look for the needle in the haystack. Just buy the haystack!
quotes.speaker: John C. Bogle
quotes.context: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing
quotes.source_title: 5 investment lessons from Vanguard founder Jack Bogle
quotes.gist: Stop trying to pick winners and simply own the whole market through an index fund.

quotes.text: My advice to the trustee could not be more simple: Put 10% of the cash in short-term government bonds and 90% in a very low-cost S&P 500 index fund.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2013 Berkshire shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2013 Annual Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: For his own heirs, Buffett prescribes a cheap S&P 500 index fund rather than picking stocks or managers.

quotes.text: I saw that with 15 to 20 good, uncorrelated return streams, I could dramatically reduce my risks without reducing expected returns.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: Principles (book), on the 'Holy Grail of Investing'
quotes.source_title: 7 learnings from Ray Dalio
