quotes.gist: Combining many uncorrelated bets cuts risk without giving up return, the closest thing to a free lunch.

quotes.text: That trust helps businesses raise the capital they need to grow, and it allows families to spread their investments across many assets at low cost instead of relying on just one.
quotes.speaker: Larry Fink
quotes.context: 2026 Annual Chairman's Letter to Investors
quotes.source_title: Larry Fink's 2026 Annual Chairman's Letter to Investors
quotes.gist: Cheap, broad diversification across many assets is a core benefit that fair markets give ordinary families.

quotes.text: A well-diversified portfolio would have somewhere between 10% and 15% in the portfolio of gold.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: Public remarks reported by TipRanks
quotes.source_title: Gold Should be 10%-15% of a 'Well-Diversified Portfolio,' Says Ray Dalio
quotes.gist: Proper diversification means holding assets beyond stocks and bonds, including a meaningful slice of gold.

quotes.text: Much of the discourse about passive investing is simply misguided.
quotes.speaker: Owen Lamont
quotes.role: Senior Vice President, Portfolio Manager, Research, Acadian Asset Management
quotes.context: Owenomics essay 'Don't Blame Indexing for Your Problems'
quotes.source_title: Don't Blame Indexing for Your Problems
quotes.gist: Fears that index funds are distorting or breaking markets are mostly wrong.

quotes.text: If you want an index fund, you can buy one with much lower costs than we or any other active investment manager apply.
quotes.speaker: Terry Smith
quotes.context: Fundsmith annual letter to shareholders
quotes.source_title: Terry Smith: Fewer companies can be run by idiots than we thought
quotes.gist: An active fund should not mimic the index; investors who want the index should simply buy a cheap one.

quotes.text: And now some people can't tell their best ideas from their worst.
quotes.speaker: Charlie Munger
quotes.context: Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting
quotes.source_title: Charles Munger: Some Investors Can't Tell Their Best Ideas From Their Worst
quotes.gist: Concentrating in your best ideas only works if you can actually tell which ideas are your best.

quotes.text: Passive investors have no opinion about value.
quotes.speaker: David Einhorn
quotes.context: Masters in Business podcast with Barry Ritholtz
quotes.source_title: Passive Investing = Broken Markets. Discuss.
quotes.gist: Index money buys regardless of price, which leaves mispricings for stock pickers and weakens markets.

quotes.text: And now passive investing has removed price discovery from the equity markets.
quotes.speaker: Michael Burry
quotes.context: Email interview with Bloomberg News
quotes.source_title: The Big Short's Michael Burry Explains Why Index Funds Are Like Subprime CDOs
quotes.gist: Index fund flows ignore fundamentals, inflating a bubble in passive investing that will end badly.

quotes.text: One's knowledge and experience are definitely limited and there are seldom more than two or three enterprises at any given time in which I personally feel myself entitled to put full confidence.
quotes.speaker: John Maynard Keynes
quotes.context: Letter to F.C. Scott
quotes.source_title: A Dozen Things I've Learned About Investing from John Maynard Keynes
quotes.gist: Only a few companies at a time deserve full confidence, so put real size into those rather than spreading thin.

quotes.text: On the other hand, if you are a know-something investor, able to understand business economics and to find five to ten sensibly-priced companies that possess important long-term competitive advantages, conventional diversification makes no sense for you.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 1993 Berkshire shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 1993 Chairman's Letter
quotes.gist: An investor who truly understands businesses should own a handful of great ones, not a diversified basket.

quotes.text: I think diversification and all the stuff they're teaching at business school today is probably the most misguided concept everywhere.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.context: Speech at the Lost Tree Club
quotes.source_title: Stanley Druckenmiller - Bulls Make Money, Bears Make Money, And Pigs Get Slaughtered - I'm Here To Tell You I Was A Pig
quotes.gist: Textbook diversification is wrong; great investors make big, concentrated bets.

quotes.text: The wise ones bet heavily when the world offers them that opportunity. They bet big when they have the odds. And the rest of the time, they don't.
quotes.speaker: Charlie Munger
quotes.context: 'A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom' talk, USC Business School
quotes.source_title: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom
quotes.gist: Wait for rare high-odds opportunities and then bet big on them instead of spreading money around.

quotes.text: History tells us that leverage all too often produces zeroes, even when it is employed by very smart people.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2010 Berkshire shareholder letter ('Life and Debt')
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2010 Annual Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: Borrowed money can wipe out even brilliant investors, so avoid leverage.

quotes.text: You wouldn't drive a car without insurance.
quotes.speaker: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
quotes.context: Interview with Institutional Investor on CalPERS dropping its tail hedge
quotes.source_title: CalPERS' Abandoned Tail Hedge Starts a War of Words
quotes.gist: A large portfolio should always carry crash insurance; dropping tail hedges is reckless.

quotes.text: But levered portfolios face a downside risk to which there isn't a corresponding upside: the risk of ruin.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo 'The Impact of Debt'
quotes.source_title: The Impact of Debt (Howard Marks memo)
quotes.gist: Leverage magnifies both ways, but it adds a one-sided danger of being wiped out.

quotes.text: I probably shouldn't say this, but when you see one cockroach, there are probably more.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: JPMorgan Q3 2025 earnings call, on credit blowups
quotes.source_title: Jamie Dimon issues private credit warning: 'When you see one cockroach, there are probably more'
quotes.gist: Early credit losses usually signal more hidden risk, so stay defensive on leveraged lending.

quotes.text: The goal of risk mitigation, like the goal of investing, should be to raise our rate of compounding over time.
quotes.speaker: Mark Spitznagel
quotes.context: Yahoo Finance interview on his book Safe Haven
quotes.source_title: Investor who returned 4,000% in Q1 2020 explains what people get wrong about risk mitigation
quotes.gist: Good crash protection should raise long-run compound returns, not just reduce volatility.

quotes.text: You shouldn't expect to make money without bearing risk, but you shouldn't expect to make money just for taking risk.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo 'The Indispensability of Risk'
quotes.source_title: The Indispensability of Risk (Howard Marks memo)
quotes.gist: Risk is necessary for returns, but taking risk alone does not guarantee being paid for it.

quotes.text: One of the hardest things to judge is what level of risk is safe.
quotes.speaker: George Soros
quotes.context: The Alchemy of Finance (book)
quotes.source_title: Diversification in the Soros Empire
quotes.gist: Sizing risk correctly is genuinely hard, cutting both ways between too much and too little.

quotes.text: Berkshire will never prefer ownership of cash-equivalent assets over the ownership of good businesses, whether controlled or only partially owned.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2024 Berkshire shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2024 Annual Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: Despite a big cash pile, owning businesses and bearing equity risk beats sitting safely in cash.

quotes.text: We terminated explicit tail-risk hedging options strategies because of their high cost, lack of scalability, and the fact that there are better alternatives available to CalPERS.
quotes.speaker: Ben Meng
quotes.context: Statement to Institutional Investor
quotes.source_title: CalPERS' Abandoned Tail Hedge Starts a War of Words
quotes.gist: Explicit tail hedges cost too much and do not scale, so a big fund is better off without them.

quotes.text: There is no way one could produce results like ours without ups and downs.
quotes.speaker: George Soros
quotes.context: Soros on Soros: Staying Ahead of the Curve (book interview with Byron Wien)
quotes.source_title: Diversification in the Soros Empire
quotes.gist: Outsized returns require accepting big swings rather than smoothing them away.

quotes.text: I strongly believe the only way to make long-term returns in our business that are superior is by being a pig.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.context: Speech at the Lost Tree Club
quotes.source_title: Stanley Druckenmiller - Bulls Make Money, Bears Make Money, And Pigs Get Slaughtered - I'm Here To Tell You I Was A Pig
quotes.gist: Superior returns come from betting very big when you have conviction.

quotes.text: As far as Soros is concerned, when you're right on something, you can't own enough.
quotes.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
quotes.role: Lead portfolio manager, Quantum Fund (Soros Fund Management)
quotes.context: The New Market Wizards (Jack Schwager interview)
quotes.source_title: Diversification in the Soros Empire
quotes.gist: When a trade is right, press it as hard as possible instead of playing it safe.

quotes.text: Our goal is to build more intelligent leverage to benefit our common stock shareholders.
quotes.speaker: Michael Saylor
quotes.context: Bloomberg Television interview
quotes.source_title: Michael Saylor Eyes 'Intelligent Leverage' to Boost MicroStrategy's Bitcoin-Driven Strategy: Bloomberg
quotes.gist: Borrowing more to buy bitcoin is a deliberate way to boost returns for shareholders.

quotes.text: People who chase growth, who chase high fliers, inevitably lose because they paid a premium price.
quotes.speaker: Seth Klarman
quotes.context: Harvard Business School alumni interview
quotes.source_title: Seth Klarman (Wikipedia)
quotes.gist: Paying up for hot growth stocks is a losing game; buy bargains instead.

quotes.text: A great company that gets expensive is much worse than a bad company that's really cheap, so you have to look at pricing.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: All-In Podcast
quotes.source_title: Ray Dalio warns investors to allocate 15% of their portfolio to gold and crypto because of skyrocketing U.S. government debt
quotes.gist: Price matters more than quality: an overpriced great company is a worse bet than a cheap bad one.

quotes.text: Buying such an issue is like betting on a topheavy favorite in a horse race.
quotes.speaker: Benjamin Graham
quotes.context: The Intelligent Investor (1949), Chapter I, p. 14
quotes.source_title: Benjamin Graham (Wikiquote)
quotes.gist: Stocks with obviously bright prospects already price them in, so buying them offers poor odds.

quotes.text: Good investing doesn't come from buying good things, but from buying things well.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo 'On Bubble Watch'
quotes.source_title: On Bubble Watch (Howard Marks memo)
quotes.gist: Returns depend on the price you pay, not on how good the company is.

quotes.text: If you're going to play the cheap game, you've got to make sure, it is armor-plated with as much quality as you can get into it.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Grantham
quotes.context: Bloomberg podcast interview, reported by MarketWatch
quotes.source_title: Jeremy Grantham on the meltdown coming for U.S. stocks and where he's putting his money now
quotes.gist: Buy cheap, but insist on quality so the bargain is not a value trap.

quotes.text: We think the very term 'value investing' is redundant. What is 'investing' if it is not the act of seeking value at least sufficient to justify the amount paid?
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 1992 Berkshire shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Value Investing: A Redundancy
quotes.gist: The value versus growth split is false; all investing is paying less than what something is worth.

quotes.text: A good investment is one in which the price is right for what the value turns out to be.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo 'The Calculus of Value'
quotes.source_title: The Calculus of Value (Howard Marks memo)
quotes.gist: Neither cheap nor expensive is good in itself; what matters is price relative to eventual value.

quotes.text: Some of the highest quality businesses in the world are trading at extremely cheap prices.
quotes.speaker: Bill Ackman
quotes.context: Post on X
quotes.source_title: Bill Ackman just gave nervous investors very good news
quotes.gist: The best setup is owning top-quality businesses when they briefly trade cheap.

quotes.text: It's far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 1989 Berkshire shareholder letter
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 1989 Chairman's Letter
quotes.gist: Paying a fair price for an excellent business beats buying a mediocre one cheaply.

quotes.text: But now that you control Berkshire, add to it wonderful businesses purchased at fair prices and give up buying fair businesses at wonderful prices.
quotes.speaker: Charlie Munger (as recounted by Warren Buffett)
quotes.context: Buffett's 2023 shareholder letter, recounting Munger's 1965 advice
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2023 Annual Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: Munger pushed Buffett away from cheap mediocre businesses toward great businesses at fair prices.

quotes.text: In my business a fourbagger is nice, but a tenbagger is the fiscal equivalent of two home runs and a double.
quotes.speaker: Peter Lynch
quotes.context: One Up on Wall Street (book), p. 32
quotes.source_title: Peter Lynch (Wikipedia)
quotes.gist: The big wins come from stocks that grow tenfold, so hunt for growth stories with that upside.

quotes.text: Conversely, if a business earns 18% on capital over 20 or 30 years, even if you pay an expensive looking price, you'll end up with a fine result.
quotes.speaker: Charlie Munger
quotes.context: 'A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom' talk, USC Business School
quotes.source_title: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom
quotes.gist: Over long horizons a high-return business rewards you even if you paid a price that looked expensive.

quotes.text: What they have in their portfolios are more value traps than they now realize, if we're right on our research.
quotes.speaker: Cathie Wood
quotes.context: Interview with ETF.com
quotes.source_title: Beware The Value Traps In Indexes
quotes.gist: Disruptive innovation is turning cheap traditional stocks into value traps, so own the disruptors instead.

quotes.text: The next big crisis in the financial markets, it's going to be private credit.
quotes.speaker: Jeffrey Gundlach
quotes.context: Bloomberg Odd Lots podcast
quotes.source_title: Jeffrey Gundlach: bond king says next financial crisis is private credit (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Gundlach names private credit, not AI, as the source of the next major financial crisis.

quotes.text: I think we are in the super-early innings of the wheels coming off the car.
quotes.speaker: Boaz Weinstein
quotes.role: Founder and CIO, Saba Capital Management
quotes.context: iConnections Global Alts conference, Miami Beach
quotes.source_title: Boaz Weinstein Warns 'Wheels Coming Off' Private Credit Funds (Bloomberg)
quotes.gist: Weinstein says the unraveling of private credit funds has only just begun.

quotes.text: When you see one cockroach, there are probably more, and so everyone should be forewarned of this one.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: JPMorgan Q3 2025 earnings call, after Tricolor and First Brands
quotes.source_title: Jamie Dimon warns of 'cockroaches' in US economy as credit concerns grow (Fox Business)
quotes.gist: Dimon warns that the first credit blowups likely signal more hidden problems to come.

quotes.text: The worst of loans are made in the best of times.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks (quoting a banking adage)
quotes.context: Memo: Cockroaches in the Coal Mine
quotes.source_title: Cockroaches in the Coal Mine (Oaktree memo)
quotes.gist: Marks argues that a long credit boom loosens standards, so the loans now coming to light were made carelessly.

quotes.text: It's a classic contagion phenomenon: 'If you can't sell what you want, you sell what you can.'
quotes.speaker: Mohamed El-Erian
quotes.role: Chief economic adviser, Allianz; President, Queens' College, Cambridge
quotes.context: Social media post after private credit funds capped withdrawals
quotes.source_title: Mohamed El-Erian says private credit stress is flashing signs of a 'classic contagion phenomenon' (Business Insider via AOL)
quotes.gist: El-Erian warns that redemption gates in private credit can force investors to dump healthy assets elsewhere.

quotes.text: Many know that in PE they're getting some serious smoothing, and a palatable (as it's way understated) reported volatility.
quotes.speaker: Cliff Asness
quotes.role: Co-founder and CIO, AQR Capital Management
quotes.context: AQR Perspective: The Illiquidity Discount?
quotes.source_title: The Illiquidity Discount? (AQR)
quotes.gist: Asness says private market marks understate true volatility, which investors knowingly accept.

quotes.text: We have seen a number of proposals from private equity funds where the returns are really not calculated in a manner that I would regard as honest.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting
quotes.source_title: Private equity's returns questioned again, this time by Buffett (Bloomberg via Daily Maverick)
quotes.gist: Buffett says private fund return figures are presented in ways he considers misleading.

quotes.text: If I were running a pension fund, I would be very careful about what was being offered to me.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting
quotes.source_title: Warren Buffett Frowns On Private Equity Performance (WealthBriefing)
quotes.gist: Buffett advises institutions to be skeptical of private fund pitches.

quotes.text: I don't think today's issues are systemic in the sense that there's something wrong with the lending system.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo: Cockroaches in the Coal Mine
quotes.source_title: Howard Marks cautions on cockroaches (Benzinga)
quotes.gist: Marks says recent credit losses reflect recurring behavior in booms, not a broken lending system.

quotes.text: I don't expect it to be systemic, but I do expect there to be problems.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: Industry conference remarks on private credit
quotes.source_title: Jamie Dimon says private credit could bring 'hell to pay' (Fortune)
quotes.gist: Dimon expects losses in private credit but not a system-wide crisis.

quotes.text: I still think it's a very good time for private credit.
quotes.speaker: Jon Gray
quotes.context: Bloomberg interview
quotes.source_title: Bloomberg: Jon Gray on Private Credit (Blackstone)
quotes.gist: Gray says the opportunity in private credit remains attractive despite the cockroach scare.

quotes.text: We believe that private markets offer the potential to enhance retirement outcomes for participants
quotes.speaker: Larry Fink
quotes.context: Annual chairman's letter to investors
quotes.source_title: Larry Fink's Annual Chairman's Letter to Investors (BlackRock)
quotes.gist: Fink argues private markets belong in ordinary retirement portfolios.

quotes.text: The vast, vast majority of private credit is investment grade.
quotes.speaker: Marc Rowan
quotes.context: Economic Club of Washington, interview with David Rubenstein
quotes.source_title: Marc Rowan Interview with David Rubenstein: Private Credit (Apollo)
quotes.gist: Rowan says private credit is mostly high-quality lending, not risky leveraged loans.

quotes.text: Lenders and bargain hunters face much better prospects in this changed environment than they did in 2009-21.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Memo: Sea Change
quotes.source_title: Sea Change (Oaktree memo)
quotes.gist: Marks argues higher rates have made lending and credit far more attractive than in the zero-rate era.

quotes.text: People have really just lost their minds, and the headlines get more and more hysterical and have almost nothing to do with the substance.
quotes.speaker: Marc Rowan
quotes.context: Apollo retirement services presentation
quotes.source_title: Rowan Says People 'Lost Their Minds' Over Private Credit Fears (Bloomberg via WealthManagement.com)
quotes.gist: Rowan dismisses private credit fears as media hysteria unconnected to fundamentals.

quotes.text: Our default rate on these types of loans is three tenths of 1%. I don't know if there's a bank around that has a default rate that's lower.
quotes.speaker: Stephen Schwarzman
quotes.context: Bloomberg interview in Tokyo
quotes.source_title: Blackstone's Schwarzman bullish on private credit (Private Equity Wire)
quotes.gist: Schwarzman says Blackstone's private loans default less than bank loans.

quotes.text: Pouring billions of dollars into China now is a tragic mistake.
quotes.speaker: George Soros
quotes.context: Wall Street Journal op-ed criticizing BlackRock's China push
quotes.source_title: George Soros says BlackRock's China investments 'tragic mistake' (Al Jazeera)
quotes.gist: Soros says investing large sums in China is a losing and dangerous bet.

quotes.text: The property crash in China will be worse than it was in America or the UK.
quotes.speaker: Jim Chanos
quotes.context: Comments on the China property bubble, reported by MoneyWeek
quotes.source_title: China's bubble will burst, and take Asia with it, says Jim Chanos (MoneyWeek)
quotes.gist: Chanos predicts China's property bust will exceed the US and UK housing crashes.

quotes.text: No one knows how far the pendulum will swing back toward the more Maoist/Marxist ways of doing things.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: LinkedIn post warning of a lost decade
quotes.source_title: Dalio says China must fix debt problems or face 'lost decade' (Hedge Fund Alpha)
quotes.gist: Dalio flags the policy risk that China drifts back toward state control.

quotes.text: You have to say, each country run by maybe a despotic authoritarian should be re-reviewed and maybe not invested in.
quotes.speaker: Kyle Bass
quotes.role: Founder and CIO, Hayman Capital Management
quotes.context: CNBC Squawk Box interview after Russia's invasion of Ukraine
quotes.source_title: Investor Kyle Bass: Globalization isn't over, just don't invest in countries run by despots (Hellenic Shipping News, via CNBC)
quotes.gist: Bass argues authoritarian markets such as China deserve to be reassessed or avoided.

quotes.text: I didn't stop to realize they're still a goddamn retailer.
quotes.speaker: Charlie Munger
quotes.role: Vice Chairman, Berkshire Hathaway; Chairman, Daily Journal
quotes.context: Daily Journal annual meeting, on the Alibaba investment
quotes.source_title: Charlie Munger called Alibaba one of the worst mistakes I ever made (Benzinga)
quotes.gist: Munger admits his Alibaba bet underrated how competitive Chinese internet retail is.

quotes.text: I have not sold anything in China yet, but I'm asking questions.
quotes.speaker: Jim Rogers
quotes.context: SFC Outlook 2026 interview, 21st Century Business Herald
quotes.source_title: SFC Outlook 2026: Legendary Investor Jim Rogers: China is one of the most promising countries (21jingji)
quotes.gist: After a strong run, Rogers is holding his China shares but questioning whether to trim.

quotes.text: I can't diversify as well as I'd like to without investing in China.
quotes.speaker: Ray Dalio
quotes.context: LinkedIn post on why he still invests in China
quotes.source_title: Billionaire investor Ray Dalio remains bullish on China despite a looming 100-year storm (Benzinga)
quotes.gist: Dalio says China is a necessary part of a well-diversified portfolio despite its risks.

quotes.text: I'm not giving up investing in China.
quotes.speaker: Jim Rogers
quotes.context: SFC Outlook 2026 interview, 21st Century Business Herald
quotes.source_title: SFC Outlook 2026: Legendary Investor Jim Rogers: China is one of the most promising countries (21jingji)
quotes.gist: Rogers remains a committed long-term investor in China.

quotes.text: So naturally, I'm willing to have some China risk in the Munger portfolio.
quotes.speaker: Charlie Munger
quotes.context: Acquired podcast interview
quotes.source_title: Charlie Munger on Buffett, gambling, Apple, and China (Morningstar India)
quotes.gist: Munger accepts China exposure because he sees better companies at lower prices.

quotes.text: I think it is excellent time - if you haven't been in emerging market bonds or high-yield bonds - to contemplate at least a partial shift based upon the level of the dollar and valuation.
quotes.speaker: Jeffrey Gundlach
quotes.context: DoubleLine investor webcast
quotes.source_title: Gundlach says excellent time for a partial shift into emerging markets (Reuters via Business Standard)
quotes.gist: Gundlach says valuations and the dollar make it a good time to rotate into emerging market debt.

quotes.text: I hope that the Chinese market collapses so I can buy Chinese shares.
quotes.speaker: Jim Rogers
quotes.context: CNBC Fast Money
quotes.source_title: Jim Rogers: China Slowdown Means Opportunity (CNBC)
quotes.gist: Rogers welcomes a Chinese selloff as a chance to buy more.

quotes.text: Everything. ETFs, I would do futures - everything. Everything.
quotes.speaker: David Tepper
quotes.context: CNBC Squawk Box, asked what to buy in China after Beijing's stimulus
quotes.source_title: David Tepper loads up on China with some very bullish comments (investingLive)
quotes.gist: Tepper says to buy every kind of China exposure after Beijing's stimulus.

quotes.text: The leading companies of China are stronger and better than practically any other leading companies anywhere, and they're available at a much cheaper price.
quotes.speaker: Charlie Munger
quotes.context: Acquired podcast interview
quotes.source_title: Charlie Munger on Buffett, gambling, Apple, and China (Morningstar India)
quotes.gist: Munger says China's top companies are world class and much cheaper than peers.

quotes.text: No one knows what oil prices will do over the next month, year, or decade.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2023 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter, on Occidental
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2023 Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: Buffett refuses to forecast oil prices even while holding a large Occidental stake.

quotes.text: We particularly like its vast oil and gas holdings in the United States, as well as its leadership in carbon-capture initiatives, though the economic feasibility of this technique has yet to be proven.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2023 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter, on Occidental
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2023 Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: Buffett values Occidental for its large US oil and gas reserves.

quotes.text: But Vicki does know how to separate oil from rock, and that's an uncommon talent, valuable to her shareholders and to her country.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.context: 2023 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter, on Occidental CEO Vicki Hollub
quotes.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway 2023 Letter to Shareholders
quotes.gist: Buffett backs Occidental on the strength of its operator rather than an oil price call.

quotes.text: Meeting rising demand will require expanding supply across oil and gas, renewables, storage, nuclear, and grids.
quotes.speaker: Larry Fink
quotes.context: Annual chairman's letter to investors, on energy pragmatism
quotes.source_title: Larry Fink's Annual Chairman's Letter to Investors (BlackRock)
quotes.gist: Fink says rising energy demand requires more oil and gas supply alongside other sources.

quotes.text: Natural gas remains essential for reliability, and the U.S. has abundant supply.
quotes.speaker: Larry Fink
quotes.context: Annual chairman's letter to investors
quotes.source_title: Larry Fink's Annual Chairman's Letter to Investors (BlackRock)
quotes.gist: Fink calls gas indispensable but notes US supply is plentiful.

quotes.text: America should lead the way in generating more energy to meet greater demand, including from AI, which will require huge amounts of energy.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: Annual letter to shareholders
quotes.source_title: JPMorgan Chase 2024 Annual Report: Chairman and CEO Letter
quotes.gist: Dimon argues AI-driven demand calls for a large expansion of US energy production.

quotes.text: The world still needs oil and natural gas today, but not all hydrocarbons are equal when it comes to their carbon footprint.
quotes.speaker: Jamie Dimon
quotes.context: Annual letter to shareholders, after Russia's invasion of Ukraine
quotes.source_title: JPMorgan Chase 2021 Annual Report: Chairman and CEO Letter
quotes.gist: Dimon says oil and gas remain necessary while favoring lower-carbon fuels.

quotes.text: Statistically, also, the level of price rises makes it extremely unlikely that the old trend is still in place.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Grantham
quotes.role: Co-founder and Chief Investment Strategist, GMO
quotes.context: GMO quarterly letter: Time to Wake Up
quotes.source_title: Time to Wake Up: Days of Abundant Resources and Falling Prices Are Over Forever (GMO)
quotes.gist: Grantham argues the century-long decline in commodity prices, oil included, has ended for good.

quotes.text: In our view, oil prices are on the threshold of a significant decline.
quotes.speaker: Cathie Wood
quotes.role: Founder, CEO and CIO, ARK Invest
quotes.context: ARK investor letter, section 'Deflation: Oil Prices'
quotes.source_title: An Investor Letter From Cathie Wood
quotes.gist: Wood argues the war-driven oil spike is near its end and prices are set to fall sharply.

quotes.text: Based on the pent-up supply built up behind the Strait of Hormuz, oil prices could drop precipitously once peace breaks out and the Strait opens.
quotes.speaker: Cathie Wood
quotes.role: Founder, CEO and CIO, ARK Invest
quotes.context: ARK investor letter
quotes.source_title: An Investor Letter From Cathie Wood
quotes.gist: Supply bottled up behind Hormuz would flood the market once the strait reopens, crushing prices.

quotes.text: The key lesson here may be that cartels and other anti-market mechanisms can’t hold forever.
quotes.speaker: Howard Marks
quotes.context: Oaktree memo 'The Lessons of Oil'
quotes.source_title: The Lessons of Oil (Oaktree memo PDF)
quotes.gist: OPEC-style price support eventually breaks, so propped-up oil prices can collapse.

quotes.text: In this testimony I will explain that Institutional Investors are one of, if not the primary, factors affecting commodities prices today.
quotes.speaker: Michael Masters
quotes.role: Managing Member and Portfolio Manager, Masters Capital Management
quotes.context: Testimony to the U.S. Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs
quotes.source_title: Testimony of Michael W. Masters before the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs
quotes.gist: A hedge fund manager argued the 2008 oil spike was inflated by index speculators rather than fundamentals.

quotes.text: Evidence that energy may be the cheapest major asset class in the world.
quotes.speaker: Leigh Goehring and Adam Rozencwajg
quotes.context: Summary of Q4 2025 commentary 'When the Strait Closed'
quotes.source_title: When the Strait Closed (Goehring & Rozencwajg 2025 Q4 commentary)
quotes.gist: The resource investors argue energy is deeply undervalued after years of capital starvation.
